data.content_ref: inline:The target treats 'the verdict-shape imposes an impossible joint requirement' as if that observation alone is the adjudication outcome, but the problem asks you to audit the critic under a named ritual whose sustained flag depends on an actual adjudication record (§11.3), not on a freestanding proof that the joint requirement is hard to meet. SRC_001 supplies no adjudication trace, no sustained-flag ledger entry, and no independent critic artifact being audited; it only re-asserts that soundness and frontier-relevance cannot be jointly guaranteed under finite evidence. That is a meta-fact about the problem's verification regime, not an audit verdict. By the ritual's own logic, if the flag were genuinely sustained it would be because the critic was caught dropping or misreporting one of the commitments during adjudication; the target instead argues that the commitments are *too hard to satisfy*, which inverts the audit direction: the auditee's difficulty is not evidence of the critic's fault. Concretely, the claim 'cannot be reliably met under finite evidence, causing persistent failure' is an unbounded empirical prediction ('persistent failure') asserted without any run data, failure log, or cited candidate set, so even on its own terms it is not a sustained finding but a conjecture presented as a verdict. Thus the target fails the problem as stated: it does not adjudicate the critic, it philosophizes about the hardness of the standard.
